senses: adj. 典型的，有代表性的；一贯的，平常的
adj. 典型的；特有的；一贯的
typical.usage: 词根:typ(模式)+ical(…的)→成为模式的→典型的；索引p418

ex.en: This meal is typical of local cookery.
ex.zh: 这是有当地风味的饭菜。

ex.en: It was typical of her to check every detail before submitting the report.
ex.zh: 提交报告前核查每一个细节，她一向如此。

ex.en: The typical household now spends a larger share of its income on housing than before.
ex.zh: 如今普通家庭花在住房上的收入比例比以前更大。

senses: a. 丑陋的；令人不快的；危险的；险恶的；凶险的
adj. 丑陋的,难看的;丑恶的,讨厌的
(大不列颠及北爱尔兰)联合王国,英国
a. 终极的；最终的；最后的
a. 最根本的；最原始的
②极点的，终极的；③基本的，根本的
ultimate.usage: ultim(最后的)+-ate→最终的；[近] final；[族]ultimately ad. 最终；根本上；[近]final a. 最终的；最后的；adj.最终的；最根本的；极限 的 n.最好的事物，最终的事物；发音类似"奥特曼的"→不到最后时刻奥特曼不会出来→最终的；词根记忆: ultim(last, 最后的)+a

ex.en: The ultimate decision lies with the parents.
ex.zh: 最后的决定权握在父母手中。

ex.en: If humanity has made some headway in realizing that the ultimate value of every institution is its distinctively human effect we may well believe that this lesson has been learned largely through dealings with the young.
ex.zh: 每个机构的最终价值在于它对人类的独特影响，如果人类在这一认识上取得一些进展的话，那么我们会完全相信这一启示主要是通过与年轻人的交往得来的。

ex.en: Reducing energy waste, not finding new supplies, is the ultimate solution to the crisis.
ex.zh: 减少能源浪费而非寻找新供应，才是这场危机的最终解决方案。

senses: adv. 最终,最后,终归;最基本地,根本上

ex.en: The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring.
ex.zh: 生活中最具挑战性的时刻是结婚、成家和最终退休。

senses: n. (尤指政治上的)极端主义者
表实物、抽象名词，名词词性

adv. 无法解释地；莫名其妙地
unaccountably.usage: adv.不可解释地；莫名其妙地；索引p418

adj. 未得到公开(或正式)承认的;非正式的
adj. 未被承认的；未被注意的
unacknowledged.usage: adj.不被承认的，未公开承认 的；索引p418

senses: a. 买不起的；负担不起的
adj. 买不起的,负担不起的

ex.en: For many young workers, housing in big cities has become simply unaffordable.
ex.zh: 对许多年轻上班族来说，大城市的住房已完全负担不起。

ex.en: Critics warn that unaffordable childcare keeps many mothers out of the labour market.
ex.zh: 批评人士警告说，负担不起的托育费用使许多母亲无法进入劳动力市场。

ex.en: Rising medical bills left the family facing unaffordable debts.
ex.zh: 不断上涨的医疗账单使这个家庭背上无力偿还的债务。

senses: adj. 全体一致的,一致同意的
unanimous.usage: un(一)+anim(精神)+ous→全体一致的；索引p418

senses: adj. 未回答的,未解答的,悬而未决的
a. 不悦目的；难看的；不好的
adj. 不悦目的,不漂亮的,难看的
adj. 不好的,无趣的,令人反感的
adj. 未经许可（或批准）的
adj. 不知道的,没意识到的,未察觉的
adj. 不知道的；没意识到的
unaware.usage: adj.不知道的；未意识到的；索引p418

senses: adv. 不能忍受地,无法容忍地
a. 无偏见的；公正的；不偏不倚的
adj. 公正的,不偏不倚的,无偏见的

ex.en: Jurors are expected to remain unbiased until all the evidence has been presented.
ex.zh: 在全部证据出示之前，陪审员应保持不偏不倚。

ex.en: Consumers trust unbiased reviews more than advertisements.
ex.zh: 消费者对公正评论的信任超过对广告的信任。

ex.en: An unbiased judge treats both sides of the dispute with equal respect.
ex.zh: 公正的法官对争议双方一视同仁。

senses: a. 异常的；难以解释的
adj. 异常的;难以解释的
adj. 不确定的,无把握的,犹豫的
a. 不可改变的；不容更改的
adj. 人迹罕至的,无人涉足的,陌生的
adj. 地图上未绘出(或未标明)的
n. 姑父；姨父；伯父；叔父；舅父

uncomfortable.usage: adj.不舒服的；尴尬的；不自在 的

unconcerned.usage: adj.不关心的；无关的；无忧虑 的

unconditional.usage: adj.无条件的，无限制的，绝 对的

senses: adj. 失去知觉的，无意识的
adj. （感情、思想等）无意识的；未察觉的；不省人事的
unconscious.usage: adj.不省人事的；无意识的， 潜意识的 n.无意识；索引p418

ex.en: Companies are using artificial intelligence to remove some of the unconscious bias from hiring decisions.
ex.zh: 公司正在利用人工智能来消除招聘决策中一些无意识的偏见。

senses: adv. 不是刻意地；没有意识到地
unconsciously.usage: adv.不知不觉；无意识地；索引p418

senses: adj. 无法控制的,难以防止的
adj. 不因循守旧的,新奇的
adj. 不时髦的,不帅的,不潇洒的
vt. 揭开,揭露;揭开……的盖子

phrases.p: uncover the origin of Hawaiian culture
phrases.m: 发现夏威夷文化的起源

senses: n. 营养不良；营养不足
adj. 秘密的，暗中进行的
v. 以低于(竞争对手)的价格销售,削弱;损害;使失败;削球
n. 底切;牛里脊肉;下旋削球

underestimate.usage: under（低）+estimate（估计）→低估。反义：overestimate vt. 高估；[近]underrate vt. 过低评价；低估；[反]overestimate vt. 高估 n. 过高的评估；组合词:under(below不足)+estimate(估算)→估算的金额不足→低估；索引p418

ex.en: It is easy to underestimate English writer James Herriot.
ex.zh: 人们很容易低估英国作家詹姆斯·赫里奥特。

ex.en: This is the well-travelled road effect: people tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a familiar route.
ex.zh: 这就是“熟悉路线效应”：人们往往会低估行驶在熟悉的路上所花费的时间。

ex.en: Never underestimate the power of a small daily habit.
ex.zh: 永远不要低估每日小习惯的力量。

undergo.usage: under（在下）+go（走）→从下面走过→经受。近义：experience vt. 经历；v.经历，经受；索引p418

ex.en: Consequently, our feelings, thoughts and emotions have undergone a corresponding change.
ex.zh: 因此，我们的感觉、思想和情绪也发生了相应的变化。

ex.en: The historic theatre will undergo careful restoration to repair damage caused by decades of neglect.
ex.zh: 这座历史悠久的剧院将接受精心修复，以治理数十年失修造成的损坏。

ex.en: Patients undergo a series of tests before doctors decide whether surgery is necessary.
ex.zh: 病人要接受一系列检查后，医生才决定是否有必要进行手术。

senses: n. 大学生,大学毕业生(c)
undergraduate.usage: [近]student n. 大学生；另：undergraduate study 本科学习；索引p418

ex.en: She teaches physics at undergraduate level.
ex.zh: 她在大学教物理。

ex.en: As an undergraduate, he published two papers in leading journals.
ex.zh: 本科期间，他就在权威期刊上发表了两篇论文。

ex.en: Undergraduate enrolment has risen sharply since tuition subsidies were introduced.
ex.zh: 自学费补贴政策出台以来，本科入学人数大幅上升。

senses: adj. 地下的,地面下的;秘密的
n. 地铁;(反抗敌人或反政府的)地下组织
underground.usage: under(在……之下)+ground(地面)→地下的；adv.在地(面)下；隐蔽地 adj.地(面)下的；秘密的，地下 的 n.地铁；地下组织；adv.在地(面)下；隐蔽地 adj.地(面)下的；秘密的，地 下的 n.地铁；(反政府的)地下组织

senses: ②引起，构成……的基础(或起因)
underlie.usage: vt.构成……的基础，为……的 起因

phrases.m: 在积极意义的词汇下画线

underline.usage: v.在……下面画线；强调，突 出 n.下划线

senses: adj. 下面的；根本的；潜在的

phrases.p: underlying generational sense of anxious urgency
phrases.m: 潜在的代际焦虑紧迫感

underlying.usage: 记：地表下层的岩浆蕴藏着潜在的能量。；联想记忆:under(在…下面)+lying(平躺的)→平躺在下面的→潜在的；索引p418

senses: vt. 逐渐削弱；暗中破坏
vt. 逐渐削弱（信心、权威等）
vt. 破坏，损害（某人的努力或成功机会）
undermine.usage: under（在下）+mine（挖）→在下面挖→暗中破坏。近义：weaken vt. 削弱；【记】under（在下面）+mine（开采）→在地表下开采矿产，导致当地居民蒙受损失→损害。近义词：stress、emphasize（强调）、weaken（削弱）；反义词：strengthen（加强）；under(在……之下)+m

ex.en: But demanding too much of air travelers or providing too little security in return undermines public support for the process.
ex.zh: 但对航空旅客要求太高，或向他们提供的安全保障太少，都会削弱公众对这一程序的支持。

ex.en: Constant criticism from managers undermines employees' confidence and eventually drives the best of them away.
ex.zh: 经理们不断的批评会削弱员工的信心，并最终把最优秀的人逼走。

senses: v. 表现不佳，业绩不佳

underscore.usage: under（在下）+score（画线）→在下面画线→强调。近义：emphasize vt. 强调

phrases.m: 使旁人理解自己的意思

senses: ad. 可以理解地；正常地；合乎情理地

understanding.usage: 记：据我了解，她是一个非常善解人意的人。；[扩]词族 understandable a. 可以理解的；[近] grasp n. 理解（力）；辨析:comprehension与understanding作理解力可通用;understanding作同情/谅解解不通用;understandable指行为可以理解

ex.en: Such an approach to education does not expand children's knowledge and understanding of the world.
ex.zh: 这样的教育方式并没有扩大孩子们对世界的认识和理解。

senses: v. 承担，担任；从事，负责
vt. 承担，从事；承诺，答应
undertake.usage: v.承担，从事；承诺，答应；under（下面）+take（拿）→从下面拿起来→扛起责任→承担。；索引p418

ex.en: The laboratory agreed to undertake a full review of the safety procedures after the accident.
ex.zh: 事故发生后，实验室同意对安全程序进行全面审查。

ex.en: Building the tunnel will require engineers to undertake one of the hardest drilling projects in Europe.
ex.zh: 修建这条隧道将要求工程师承担欧洲难度最高的钻探工程之一。

ex.en: The government undertook to halve carbon emissions within fifteen years, though experts doubted the timetable.
ex.zh: 政府承诺在十五年内将碳排放减半，不过专家们对这一时间表表示怀疑。

senses: v. 低估，轻视；对……认识不足
undervalue.usage: v.低估……的价值；看轻，轻视 n.低于实际价值的价格；under（少于）+value（估价）→估价少了→低估

ex.en: He believes his house has been undervalued.
ex.zh: 他认为自己的房子估值太低。

senses: adj. 不想要的,不得人心的
n. 不受欢迎的人,不良分子
adj. 不想要的；不得人心的；易惹麻烦的
undesirable.usage: adj.不受欢迎的，不良的，不 想要的 n.不良分子，不受欢迎的人；desirable 的派生词

senses: adj. 未开垦的,未开发的,未利用的
adj. 未开发的，未发展的
a. 未分心的，注意力集中的
vt. 解开，打开；取消，废除
undo.usage: 派生undoing n.失败或覆灭的原因;undone adj.已打开的;过去式undid；索引p418

senses: adj. 无疑的,确实的,千真万确的

phrases.m: 毋庸置疑的和值得尊敬的地位

undoubtedly.usage: 记：这件事无疑是成功的，他的怀疑是多余的。；adv.无疑，肯定；索引p418

ex.en: Even so, kings and queens undoubtedly have a downside.
ex.zh: 即便如此，国王和女王无疑都有不足之处。

ex.en: Handwriting is undoubtedly slower than typing, but it may deepen memory.
ex.zh: 手写无疑比打字慢，但可能加深记忆。

ex.en: The discovery undoubtedly ranks among the major breakthroughs of the century.
ex.zh: 这一发现无疑是本世纪最重大的突破之一。

senses: adj. ①心神不宁的，不安宁的
adj. 心神不安的，担心的
uneasy.usage: adj.担忧的，不安的；令人不 舒服的

ex.en: Many employees felt uneasy about the sudden change of management.
ex.zh: 许多员工对管理层的突然变动感到不安。

ex.en: The uneasy silence in the room suggested that something had gone wrong.
ex.zh: 房间里令人不安的沉默表明出了问题。

ex.en: She grew uneasy when her son failed to answer his phone all night.
ex.zh: 儿子整晚不接电话，她越来越担心。

senses: adj. 不赢利的,不赚钱的;不合算的,不经济的
adj. 不赢利的；不划算的
a. 失业的；下岗的；待业的
adj. 失业的,待业的,下岗的
adj. 失业的；未被利用的
unemployed.usage: adj.未被雇用的，失业的；索引p418

ex.en: The recession left thousands of skilled workers unemployed.
ex.zh: 经济衰退使数千名技术工人失业。

ex.en: Government programmes offer free training to the unemployed.
ex.zh: 政府项目为失业者提供免费培训。

ex.en: After the factory closed, nearly a third of the town's workforce was unemployed.
ex.zh: 工厂关闭后，该镇近三分之一的劳动力失去了工作。

senses: n. 失业；失业人数；无业
n. 失业；失业率；失业人数
unemployment.usage: [扩]词族 employ vt. 雇用；[反] employment n. 就业；n.失业人数；失业，失业状态；索引p418

ex.en: Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
ex.zh: 加拿大和其他地方的努力可以说是迟缓乏力的，这使我们陷入一种境地：我们经常听到雇主苦苦寻求工人，即使在失业率高的时期和地区也是如此。

ex.en: Youth unemployment remains high even in regions where employers complain that they cannot find workers.
ex.zh: 即使在雇主抱怨招不到工人的地区，青年失业率依然高企。

ex.en: Automation could push unemployment higher unless workers are retrained for new kinds of jobs.
ex.zh: 除非对工人进行再培训以适应新型工作，否则自动化可能推高失业率。

senses: a. 不平坦的；不规则的；不均衡的
adj. 凹凸不平的,不平坦的;不规则的,无规律的
adj. 不均衡的,不公平的,不稳定的,不连续的;实力悬殊的;不在同一水平的
adj. 不均匀的；不平坦的；不平等的

ex.en: The report found that economic recovery has been uneven across different regions of the country.
ex.zh: 报告发现，该国不同地区的经济复苏并不均衡。

ex.en: The old pavement was uneven, so pedestrians had to walk carefully along the street.
ex.zh: 旧人行道凹凸不平，行人沿街行走时不得不小心。

ex.en: Teachers complained that the distribution of educational resources remained highly uneven between urban and rural schools.
ex.zh: 教师们抱怨城乡学校之间的教育资源分配仍然极不均衡。

senses: a. 想不到的，意外的，突然的
unexpected.usage: [扩]词族 unexpectedly ad. 出人意料地；[近] sudden a. 突然的；索引p418

ex.en: The company's sudden collapse came as an unexpected blow to thousands of employees and investors.
ex.zh: 该公司突然倒闭，对数千名员工和投资者来说是一个意外打击。

ex.en: An unexpected increase in oil prices pushed up the cost of living in many importing countries.
ex.zh: 石油价格的意外上涨推高了许多进口国的生活成本。

ex.en: Scientists were surprised by the unexpected results of the experiment, which contradicted the accepted theory.
ex.zh: 科学家们对这项与公认理论相矛盾的实验意外结果感到惊讶。

senses: adv. 出乎意料地，意外地
a. 不公平的；不公正的

ex.en: Workers went on strike to protest against the unfairness of the new pay system.
ex.zh: 工人们举行罢工，抗议新薪酬制度的不公正。

ex.en: Many parents believe that the unfairness of the entrance exam discourages students from poor families.
ex.zh: 许多家长认为，入学考试的不公平使贫困家庭的学生气馁。

ex.en: The court's decision was criticized for the obvious unfairness of its treatment of the two parties.
ex.zh: 该裁决因对双方的处理明显不公而受到批评。

senses: adj. 陌生的,不熟悉的,不认识的
adj. 不时兴的,不时髦的,过时的

ex.en: The idea of saving cash in a bank account now seems unfashionable among young investors.
ex.zh: 把钱存在银行账户的想法如今在年轻投资者中显得不合时宜。

ex.en: He deliberately wears unfashionable clothes to show his indifference to trends.
ex.zh: 他故意穿着过时的衣服，以显示自己对潮流的漠视。

ex.en: Critics claimed the professor's theories had become unfashionable but were far from disproved.
ex.zh: 批评者称这位教授的理论已经过时，但远未被证伪。

unfavorable.usage: adj.不宜的；令人不快的；不 赞成的

senses: adj. 不利的,有害的;不赞同的

phrases.m: 遵循不利的资产评估准则

senses: a. 不可行的；难以实现的
adj. 不可行的;难以实现的

ex.en: Engineers concluded that building a bridge at this site was technically unfeasible because of the soft soil.
ex.zh: 工程师们得出结论，由于土质松软，在此处建桥在技术上不可行。

ex.en: The plan to cut costs by half within a month proved unfeasible and was eventually abandoned.
ex.zh: 一个月内将成本削减一半的计划被证明不可行，最终被放弃。

ex.en: Critics argued that the government's housing scheme was financially unfeasible in the long run.
ex.zh: 批评者指出，政府的住房计划从长远来看在财政上不可行。

senses: adj. 贬损的；不敢恭维的
adj. 漫不经心的,目的不明确的,组织不严密的,松散的

unfold.usage: un（不）+fold（折叠）→不再折叠→展开。反义：fold v. 折叠；辨析:unfold把折叠或卷起来的东西打开,与fold相对;open把关闭或封起来的东西打开,与close相对

ex.en: Unfortunately, life is not a bed of roses.
ex.zh: 不幸的是，生活不是安乐窝。

ex.en: The funding was approved; unfortunately, the project team had already been disbanded.
ex.zh: 经费获批了；遗憾的是，项目团队已经解散。

ex.en: Unfortunately for the publishers, readers showed little interest in the new electronic format.
ex.zh: 对出版商来说遗憾的是，读者对这种新电子格式兴趣寥寥。

ex.en: The unification of the two countries opened a new chapter in the history of the region.
ex.zh: 两国的统一开启了该地区历史的新篇章。

ex.en: Economic unification requires member states to give up some of their independent policy-making power.
ex.zh: 经济统一要求成员国放弃部分独立的政策制定权。

ex.en: The unification of Germany fundamentally changed the political landscape of Europe.
ex.zh: 德国的统一从根本上改变了欧洲的政治格局。

senses: adj. 不变的,相同的,均匀的,统一的
uniform.usage: 派生uniformity n.统一,一律,一致性；n.制服，校服 adj.全部相同的，始终如一的；uni（统一的）+form（形式）→统一形式的衣服→校服；索引p418

ex.en: Growth has not been uniform across the country.
ex.zh: 全国各地的发展程度不一。

ex.en: The school requires every student to wear a dark blue uniform on formal occasions.
ex.zh: 学校要求每个学生在正式场合穿深蓝色制服。

ex.en: The temperature of the storage room must be kept at a uniform level to protect the instruments.
ex.zh: 储藏室的温度必须保持在恒定水平，以保护仪器。

ex.en: Critics argue that standardized tests impose a uniform standard on children with very different talents.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，标准化考试把统一的标准强加给天赋迥异的孩子们。

uniformly.usage: adv.一致地，均匀地；adv.一致地；索引p418

ex.en: The reviews of the new policy were not uniformly positive; several experts expressed strong doubts.
ex.zh: 对新政策的评价并非一致正面，几位专家表达了强烈怀疑。

ex.en: The material must be heated uniformly, otherwise it will crack under the sudden change of temperature.
ex.zh: 材料必须均匀加热，否则会因温度骤变而开裂。

ex.en: Studies show that the drug is not uniformly effective across all groups of patients.
ex.zh: 研究表明，这种药物对所有患者群体的疗效并不一致。

ex.en: The new leader hopes to unify the country.
ex.zh: 新领袖希望把国家统一起来。

ex.en: A common language can help unify diverse groups within a multilingual society.
ex.zh: 共同的语言有助于统一多语社会中的不同群体。

ex.en: The company introduced a single software platform to unify its operations across all branches.
ex.zh: 公司引入了统一的软件平台，以统一所有分支机构的运营。

ex.en: Sports events sometimes have the power to unify people who differ in politics and religion.
ex.zh: 体育赛事有时具有团结政治与宗教信仰各异的人们的力量。

ex.en: In response to these many unilateral measures, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) is currently working with 131 countries to reach a consensus by the end of 2020 on an international solution.
ex.zh: 为了应对这些单边措施，经济合作与发展组织(OECD)目前正与131个国家合作，以期在2020年年底之前就一项国际解决方案达成共识。

senses: adj. 难以置信的,不可想象的

unimpressive.usage: adj.无印象的；给人印象不深的

senses: n. 结合，联合；工会，联盟
union.usage: 串词记忆：洋葱(onion)协会(union)；①联盟（另：the International Union for the Conservation of Nature 世界自然保护联盟）②协会；索引p418

ex.en: She became active in the teachers' union.
ex.zh: 她在教师工会中变得活跃起来。

ex.en: The union is pressing the management for safer working conditions.
ex.zh: 工会正在敦促资方提供更安全的工作条件。

ex.en: Marriage should be a union of two equals rather than a business deal.
ex.zh: 婚姻应是两个平等个体的结合，而不是一桩交易。

senses: n. [U] 联合主义；统一主义
vt.&vi. 组织(或成立)工会；(使)加入工会
v. 组织(或成立)工会;(使)加入工会
a. 独一无二的；独特的
adj. 唯一的，独一无二的
adj. 独一无二的；独特的；独有的
unique.usage: 无比较级。近义：unparalleled a. 无与伦比的；adj.独一无二的，独特的；索引p418

ex.en: Every person's fingerprint is unique, which makes it a reliable means of identification.
ex.zh: 每个人的指纹都是独一无二的，因此是指认身份的可靠手段。

ex.en: The island's unique wildlife attracts scientists from around the world.
ex.zh: 这座岛屿独特的野生动物吸引着世界各地的科学家。

ex.en: The museum offers a unique opportunity to see original manuscripts.
ex.zh: 这座博物馆提供了观赏手稿真迹的难得机会。

ex.en: Environmental groups united to pressure the government into tightening pollution controls.
ex.zh: 环保团体联合起来，迫使政府加强污染管制。

ex.en: The crisis united the two political parties in support of the emergency plan.
ex.zh: 这场危机使两党联合起来支持紧急计划。

ex.en: Workers from different factories united to demand better working conditions and higher wages.
ex.zh: 来自不同工厂的工人联合起来，要求改善工作条件并提高工资。

senses: n. [U,sing.] 团结一致；统一；联合
unity.usage: 记：各族人民联合起来共同维护国家的统一。；助记:uni(唯一)+ty(名词后缀)→唯一→一致；n.团结，统一；整体性，统一性； 统一体

ex.en: The design lacks unity.
ex.zh: 这项设计整体不够协调。

ex.en: The crisis brought a rare sense of unity to the divided parliament.
ex.zh: 这场危机给分裂的议会带来了一种罕见的团结感。

ex.en: Economic unity among the member states was the founding goal of the bloc.
ex.zh: 成员国之间的经济联合是该集团的创立目标。

senses: adj. ①普遍的，全体的，通用的
universal.usage: 辨析:universal毫无例外涉及整体中个体,常修饰真理法则;common为群体全员共享共用;general一般的,含例外较少之意；① adj. 普遍（存在）的（2015年完形）；索引p418

ex.en: This universal protection sends the message: "Please don't approach me."
ex.zh: 这种普遍的自我保护传递出这样的信息："请不要靠近我。"

ex.en: There is no universal formula for success; strategies must be adapted to local conditions.
ex.zh: 成功没有放之四海而皆准的公式，策略必须因地制宜。

ex.en: The desire for a better life seems to be a universal human aspiration across cultures.
ex.zh: 对美好生活的向往似乎是跨文化的人类普遍愿望。

ex.en: Critics doubt whether a universal basic income can be sustained by most national economies.
ex.zh: 批评者怀疑大多数国家的经济能否维持全民基本收入。

ex.en: Astronomers continue to explore how the universe expanded in the first moments after the Big Bang.
ex.zh: 天文学家继续探索宇宙在大爆炸后的最初时刻是如何膨胀的。

ex.en: Modern physics suggests that the universe is far larger and stranger than we once imagined.
ex.zh: 现代物理学表明，宇宙比我们曾经想象的要大得多、奇特得多。

ex.en: The telescope allows scientists to observe galaxies at the edge of the known universe.
ex.zh: 这台望远镜使科学家能够观测到已知宇宙边缘的星系。

senses: adj. 不公平的,不公正的,非正义的
adj. 无法知道的,不可知的

ex.en: Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.
ex.zh: 直觉的特殊力量只有在特定的情况下才会被释放出来。

ex.en: The U.S. Supreme Court frowns on sex-based classifications unless they are designed to address an "important" policy interest.
ex.zh: 美国最高法院不允许基于性别的分类，除非这些分类是设计来解决"重要的"政策利益问题。

ex.en: Small businesses cannot survive in the digital market unless they adapt quickly to new technologies.
ex.zh: 小企业若不迅速适应新技术，就无法在数字市场中生存。

ex.en: Unless governments invest more in public transport, traffic congestion will continue to worsen.
ex.zh: 除非政府加大对公共交通的投资，否则交通拥堵将继续恶化。

ex.en: The experiment cannot be repeated unless the original conditions are precisely recorded.
ex.zh: 除非精确记录原始条件，否则实验无法重复。

unlike.usage: [扩][近] different a. 不同的；[反] alike a. 相像

ex.en: They are both teachers. Otherwise they are quite unlike.
ex.zh: 他们两位都是教师。除此之外他们迥然不同。

ex.en: Unlike traditional classrooms, online courses allow students to learn at their own pace.
ex.zh: 与传统课堂不同，在线课程允许学生按自己的节奏学习。

ex.en: Unlike his colleagues, he welcomed criticism as a chance to improve his research.
ex.zh: 与同事不同，他把批评当作改进研究的机会。

ex.en: The climate of the southern coast is mild, unlike the harsh winters of the inland regions.
ex.zh: 南部沿海气候温和，与内陆地区严酷的冬季不同。

senses: adj. 未必的，靠不住的，不像的
adj. 不大可能发生的；非心目中的

phrases.p: in the unlikely event of sth.

unlikely.usage: [扩][近] improbable a. 不大可能的；[反] likely a. 可能的；adj.不太可能的；未必真实的 adv.未必；索引p419

ex.en: It is unlikely that the company will recover from the scandal before the year ends.
ex.zh: 该公司不太可能在年底前从这场丑闻中恢复过来。

ex.en: She is an unlikely candidate for the job, having never studied marketing.
ex.zh: 她从未学过营销，不太像能胜任这份工作的人选。

ex.en: In such a dry season, heavy rain seems most unlikely.
ex.zh: 在如此干燥的季节里，出现强降雨的可能性微乎其微。

phrases.m: 一所不知名的私立大学

senses: adj. 不自然的,反常的,勉强的
adj. 反常的；不自然的；勉强的
adv. 不需要地,不必地,多余地

unnecessary.usage: adj.不必要的；多余的，无用 的；索引p419

senses: a. 无与伦比的；空前的
unparalleled.usage: unique 的近义词；adj.无比的；前所未有的；独特 的

senses: adj. 前所未有的,没有先例的
unprecedented.usage: adj.前所未有的，史无前例的；索引p419

ex.en: Writing for the National Immigration Forum, Gregory Rodriguez reports that today's immigration is neither at unprecedented levels nor resistant to assimilation.
ex.zh: 格雷戈里·罗德里格斯在为“国家移民论坛”撰稿时写道，如今的移民既未达到前所未有的水平，也不排斥同化。

ex.en: The pandemic placed unprecedented pressure on hospitals and supply chains around the world.
ex.zh: 疫情给世界各地的医院和供应链带来了前所未有的压力。

ex.en: The speed of urbanization in developing countries is unprecedented in human history.
ex.zh: 发展中国家城市化的速度在人类历史上是前所未有的。

ex.en: The court's ruling set an unprecedented precedent for cases involving digital privacy.
ex.zh: 法院的裁决为涉及数字隐私的案件开创了前所未有的先例。

senses: n. 不可预测,难以预料
unpredictability.usage: n.不可预测性，不可预知性

ex.en: Farmers suffer most from the unpredictability of extreme weather caused by climate change.
ex.zh: 农民受气候变化导致的极端天气不可预测性的影响最大。

ex.en: The unpredictability of market movements makes long-term financial planning extremely difficult.
ex.zh: 市场波动的不可预测性使长期财务规划极为困难。

ex.en: Investors demand higher returns to compensate for the unpredictability of political risks.
ex.zh: 投资者要求更高的回报，以补偿政治风险的不可预测性。

senses: a. 难以预料的；(人)善变的，难以捉摸的
adj. 无法预言的,不可预测的,难以预料的
adj. 不可预测的，难以预料的
unpredictable.usage: adj.无法预测的，不定的；(人) 善变的；索引p419

ex.en: The weather in the mountains is highly unpredictable, so climbers must be well prepared.
ex.zh: 山区的天气极难预料，因此登山者必须做好充分准备。

ex.en: Investors dislike unpredictable policies because they make long-term planning almost impossible.
ex.zh: 投资者不喜欢难以预测的政策，因为那几乎使长期规划无法进行。

ex.en: His unpredictable temper made his colleagues cautious around him.
ex.zh: 他那难以捉摸的脾气使同事们在他们面前小心谨慎。

senses: adj. 无准备的；不乐意的
adj. 谦虚谨慎的,不事张扬的
adj. 不切实际的,不实事求是的
unrealistic.usage: adj.不切实际的；不实在的 Clone 已经成为了一个trend，克隆experiment 的成功将会对社会有potential 的impact，thus，克隆的 advocates 认为，choose 克隆可以成为gain happin

senses: adj. 不合理的;不公正的;期望过高的
adj. 未被意识到的；被忽略的
adj. 未被意识到的,被忽略的,不受重视的
a. 不思考的；缺乏考虑的；不反射的
adj. 无关联的,不相关的,无亲缘关系的
adj. 不相关的；无亲属关系的

ex.en: The two events may appear unrelated, but a closer look reveals a common cause.
ex.zh: 这两起事件看似互不相关，但细看之下会发现共同的原因。

ex.en: The witness mentioned several details unrelated to the case.
ex.zh: 证人提到了几个与案件无关的细节。

ex.en: She spends her weekends on hobbies entirely unrelated to her job.
ex.zh: 她周末的爱好与工作完全无关。

senses: a. 无代表性的；不典型的
adj. 不典型的,无代表性的
adj. 不典型的；无代表性的

ex.en: Critics claim that the survey sample was too small and therefore unrepresentative of the whole population.
ex.zh: 批评者称调查样本太小，因而无法代表全体人口。

ex.en: Politicians chosen by party leaders may be unrepresentative of ordinary party members.
ex.zh: 由政党领袖挑选的政客可能无法代表普通党员。

ex.en: The study warns that data collected from online users is often unrepresentative of society at large.
ex.zh: 该研究警告说，从网络用户收集的数据往往无法代表整个社会。

senses: adj. 无反应的；反应迟钝的
v. 解除职务;赶下台;使掉下马(或自行车)
v. 使心神不宁;扰乱;使担忧
unsettle.usage: adj.不平稳的；不安的；未解 决的；索引p419

ex.en: Rumors of further layoffs unsettled the employees and lowered productivity across the department.
ex.zh: 进一步裁员的谣言使员工人心惶惶，降低了整个部门的生产率。

ex.en: Sudden changes in interest rates can unsettle financial markets and discourage long-term investment.
ex.zh: 利率的突然变化会扰乱金融市场，抑制长期投资。

ex.en: The unexplained noises in the old house unsettled the new residents within days.
ex.zh: 老房子里无法解释的声响在几天内就使新住户心神不宁。

senses: adj. 未破解的，未解决的

unstable.usage: adj.不稳定的；动荡的；易变的

senses: adj. 未经试验(或考验)的
adj. 不平常的，与众不同的
adj. 笨拙的;笨重的;不灵便的;无效率的;臃肿的

unwilling.usage: adj.不愿意的；不情愿的；勉强 的；索引p419

senses: adv. 不知情地，未意识到地
a. 不值得的；不相称的；格格不入的
adj. 不值得(尊重)的;不配的;格格不入的
adj. 不能接受的;(与……的身份)不相称的
unworthy.usage: adj.不值得的；无价值的；不 相称的；索引p419

ex.en: Such rude behaviour is unworthy of a well-educated man.
ex.zh: 如此粗鲁的行为与一个受过良好教育的人不相称。

ex.en: He felt unworthy of the honour the university had conferred on him.
ex.zh: 他觉得自己配不上大学授予他的荣誉。

ex.en: Critics argued that the project was unworthy of public funding.
ex.zh: 批评者认为该项目不值得用公共资金资助。

senses: 表有……性质的，形容词词性
adj. 时新的,新式的,现代化的

ex.en: Doctors rely on up-to-date research to choose the most effective treatment for each patient.
ex.zh: 医生依靠最新研究为每位患者选择最有效的治疗方案。

ex.en: The library provides students with up-to-date computers and free access to online databases.
ex.zh: 图书馆为学生提供最新的计算机和免费的在线数据库访问。

ex.en: Keeping the safety regulations up to date is essential as new technologies enter the workplace.
ex.zh: 随着新技术进入工作场所，使安全法规保持最新至关重要。

senses: adj. 即将发生(或来临)的

ex.en: Upcoming reforms might bring the price to a more reasonable level.
ex.zh: 未来的改革可能会使价格达到一个更合理的水平。

senses: adj. 坦率的,诚实的,直爽的;预付的,预交的
v. 使(机器、计算机系统等)升级；使升舱；使(旅馆房间等)升级
upgrade.usage: up（向上）+grade（等级）→向上提级→升级。反义：downgrade vt. 使降级；up(往上)+grade(等级)→使你的等级往上升→升级；词根记忆: up(向上)+grad(go, 走)→向上走→升级；索引p419

ex.en: As an executive coach, I've seen image upgrades be particularly helpful during transitions.
ex.zh: 作为一名管理人员培训师，我发现在过渡时期提升形象特别有帮助。

ex.en: Auto companies will upgrade the design of their vehicles.
ex.zh: 汽车公司将升级车辆的设计。

ex.en: Passengers can pay a small fee for an upgrade to business class.
ex.zh: 乘客只需支付少量费用即可升舱至商务舱。

senses: v. 维护，支持；维持；受理（申诉）
vt. 维持（原判、裁决等）；维护（法律、正义等）
uphold.usage: 同义:support,maintain；v.支持，维护；维持；up（往上）+hold（拿）→朝上拿着→举起→支持。；索引p419

ex.en: The justices signaled that too many patents were being upheld for "inventions" that are obvious.
ex.zh: 法官们表示太多专利授给了平淡无奇的“发明”。

ex.en: On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move.
ex.zh: 周二，该上诉法院一致支持2017年放宽对宽带供应商进行管制的规定，并援引了最高法院2005年的一项裁决，该裁决维持了类似的放宽管制举措。

ex.en: The Supreme Court upheld the lower court's decision by a narrow majority.
ex.zh: 最高法院以微弱多数维持了下级法院的裁决。

ex.en: Every citizen has a duty to uphold the law rather than challenge it on the streets.
ex.zh: 每个公民都有维护法律的义务，而不是在大街上挑战法律。

senses: v. 给(家具)装上软垫(或套子)
n. 供养(费);维修(费);保养(费)

ex.en: Users can upload their photos to the cloud and share them with friends within seconds.
ex.zh: 用户可以把照片上传到云端，并在几秒钟内与朋友分享。

ex.en: The platform requires teachers to upload their course materials before the semester begins.
ex.zh: 该平台要求教师在学期开始前上传课程资料。

ex.en: Millions of videos are uploaded to the Internet every day, posing challenges for content review.
ex.zh: 每天有数百万视频被上传到互联网，给内容审核带来挑战。

senses: adj. 上面的,上部的,较高的

ex.en: Moreover, even though humans have been upright for millions of years, our feet and back continue to struggle with bipedal posture and cannot easily withstand repeated strain imposed by oversize limbs.
ex.zh: 而且，尽管人类已经直立行走了几百万年，但为了保持两足直立的姿势我们的双脚和背部已经勉为其难了，实在难以再轻易承受过长的四肢所带来的持续重压。

ex.en: The ancient stone pillars have remained upright for more than two thousand years.
ex.zh: 这些古老的石柱已直立两千多年。

ex.en: Walking upright freed our ancestors' hands for making tools and carrying food.
ex.zh: 直立行走解放了祖先的双手，使他们能够制造工具和搬运食物。

ex.en: He was widely respected as an upright judge who refused all bribes and personal favors.
ex.zh: 他作为一位拒绝一切贿赂和人情的正直法官而广受尊敬。

senses: a. 失望的，苦恼的；n. 肠胃病
upset.usage: up（向上）+set（放）→被翻起来→打乱；【记】up（增多）+set（使开始）→使某人的怒气开始增多→使生气。拓展：upsetting a. 令人不快的；近义词：annoy vt. 使生气；同义:disturb,distress,spoil;overturn,overthrow；发音类似"俺不赛"→俺很郁闷不想参加比

ex.en: If it is trying to upset Google, it has chosen an indirect method.
ex.zh: 如果它是在试图惹恼谷歌，那么它选择了一种间接的方法。

ex.en: Elisabeth was upset by the consequences of the current sorting mechanism.
ex.zh: 伊丽莎白对现行的社会分选机制感到失望。

ex.en: The delay in delivering the goods upset the whole production schedule.
ex.zh: 交货延迟打乱了整个生产计划。

senses: n. (糟糕局面的)好的一面,光明的一面,正面
upside.usage: n.好的一面 prep.对着……一侧；索引p419

ex.en: The upside of working from home is that employees save hours of commuting time every week.
ex.zh: 居家办公的好处是员工每周可以节省数小时的通勤时间。

ex.en: Despite the risks, investors saw a considerable upside in the emerging technology sector.
ex.zh: 尽管有风险，投资者仍看到新兴科技行业相当大的上行潜力。

ex.en: Every failure has an upside: it teaches lessons that success can rarely offer.
ex.zh: 每次失败都有好的一面：它教给人们成功难以提供的教训。

senses: n. 自命不凡的新上任者;狂妄自大的新手

upward.usage: adj.升高的，上升的；向上的 adv.向上；上升地

ex.en: Housing prices have shown a steady upward trend since the beginning of the year.
ex.zh: 自年初以来，房价呈现稳步上升的趋势。

ex.en: The economy is expected to move upward as consumer confidence gradually recovers.
ex.zh: 随着消费者信心逐渐恢复，经济预计将上行。

ex.en: She gave him an upward glance before continuing to type her report.
ex.zh: 她向上看了他一眼，然后继续打字写报告。

senses: adj. 城市的；都市的；城镇的；城市音乐的
urban.usage: adj.城市的，城镇的；住在都 市的；ur（鹅）+ban（禁止）→禁止养鹅，一般在城市里有限制或禁令→城市的；都市的。

ex.en: Today, as urban population explodes globally, cities become more crowded.
ex.zh: 今天，随着全球城市人口激增，城市变得更加拥挤。

ex.en: More than half of the world's population now lives in urban areas.
ex.zh: 如今世界一半以上的人口居住在城市地区。

ex.en: Urban planning experts warn that poor design can deepen social inequality.
ex.zh: 城市规划专家警告说，糟糕的设计会加剧社会不平等。

senses: 表示行为或行为的结果，名词词性

phrases.p: urge sb. to do/into doing sth.

urge.usage: urg(驱赶)+e→驱赶去做→催促；[族] urgent a. 紧急的；发音类似“我急”→我非常着急，所以“催促”大家快点做事。；索引p419

ex.en: Self-expression is a basic human urge.
ex.zh: 自我表达是人类的一种基本欲望。

ex.en: He also urged councils to impose "fast-food-free zones" around schools and hospitals—areas within which takeaways cannot open.
ex.zh: 他还敦促委员会在学校周边和医院周边设置"无快餐区域"，在该区域内不能开设外卖餐馆。

ex.en: One of these urges has to do with creating a state of peace in the midst of turbulence, a "still point of the turning world," to borrow a phrase from T. S. Eliot.
ex.zh: 在这众多的欲求中，其中一种就与如何在喧嚣中营造出一种宁静的状态有关，借用T.S.艾略特的话来说就是一个"旋转世界中的静点"。

urgency.usage: urgent 的派生词；n.紧急，迫切；索引p419

ex.en: Climate scientists stress the urgency of cutting carbon emissions within the next decade.
ex.zh: 气候科学家强调在未来十年内减排的紧迫性。

ex.en: The doctor explained the urgency of the operation to the patient's family in simple words.
ex.zh: 医生用通俗的语言向病人家属说明了手术的紧迫性。

ex.en: There is growing urgency among policymakers to reform the outdated tax system.
ex.zh: 决策者对改革过时税制的感觉日益紧迫。

phrases.p: be urgent for sb. to do sth.
be urgent with sb. for sth.

urgent.usage: urg(驱赶)+-ent→被驱赶的→紧急的；[族] urgency n. 紧急；urge v. 催促；族：urgency n. 紧急；催促。近义：pressing a. 紧迫的；adj.紧急的；急切的；索引p419

ex.en: They could still invalidate Fourth Amendment protections when facing severe, urgent circumstances, and they could take reasonable measures to ensure that phone data are not erased or altered while a warrant is pending.
ex.zh: 面临严峻紧急局势,他们依然会使第四修正案所提供的保护不具效力,他们会在等待法律授权的时间内采取合理措施来确保手机数据不会被删除或是更改。

ex.en: The hospital admitted the patient at once because his condition was urgent.
ex.zh: 医院立即收治了这名病人，因为他的情况紧急。

ex.en: Climate scientists warn that urgent action is needed to cut carbon emissions within a decade.
ex.zh: 气候科学家警告说，十年之内需要采取紧急行动减少碳排放。

ex.en: The manager cancelled all other meetings to deal with an urgent matter raised by the board.
ex.zh: 经理取消了所有其他会议，以处理董事会提出的一项紧急事务。

ex.en: The dictionary records changes in word usage over the past fifty years.
ex.zh: 这部词典记录了过去五十年间词语用法的变化。

ex.en: Heavy usage of the network during peak hours often slows down the connection.
ex.zh: 高峰时段网络的繁重使用常常使连接变慢。

ex.en: The manual explains the correct usage of each function with clear examples.
ex.zh: 手册用清晰的例子解释了每个功能的正确用法。

senses: vt. 使用；利用；运用；消耗

ex.en: The problem with open-source AI art generators is that they make unauthorized use of online images.
ex.zh: 开源人工智能艺术生成器的问题在于它们在未经授权的情况下使用网络图片。

ex.en: Researchers must use evidence rather than intuition when evaluating a new medical treatment.
ex.zh: 研究人员在评估新疗法时必须依据证据而非直觉。

ex.en: The museum makes creative use of digital technology to bring ancient paintings to life.
ex.zh: 博物馆创造性地利用数字技术使古代绘画栩栩如生。

ex.en: Companies that use customer data responsibly tend to earn greater public trust.
ex.zh: 负责任地使用客户数据的公司往往能赢得更多公众信任。

senses: a. 二手的；用过的；旧的
adj. 用旧了的,用过的;(to)习惯于……的
used.usage: get/be used to sth./to doing sth. 指习惯于（做）某事；used to do sth 指过去常常做某事，但现在不做了；索引p419

ex.en: She used to commute two hours a day before the company allowed remote work.
ex.zh: 在公司允许远程办公之前，她过去每天要通勤两小时。

ex.en: Older employees are used to paper records, so the new digital system confused them at first.
ex.zh: 年长员工习惯于纸质记录，因此起初对新数字系统感到困惑。

ex.en: The second-hand market has grown rapidly as more consumers buy used furniture to save money.
ex.zh: 随着更多消费者购买二手家具以省钱，二手市场迅速增长。

senses: a. 有用的；有益的；实用的；有帮助的
useful.usage: 反义useless adj.无用的,无益的；索引p419

ex.en: The training course provides useful skills that graduates can immediately apply at work.
ex.zh: 培训课程提供毕业生能够立即在工作中应用的实用技能。

ex.en: Feedback from customers is useful for improving both products and services.
ex.zh: 客户的反馈对改进产品和服务都很有用。

ex.en: It is useful to compare several studies before drawing a conclusion from the data.
ex.zh: 在从数据中得出结论之前，比较多项研究是有益的。

senses: n. 引座员;招待员;门房;助理教员
a. 通常的；寻常的；惯常的
ad. 通常地；正常地；一般地；经常地
v. 利用；使用；运用；应用
utilise.usage: 美拼写utilize；书中亦作utilize/-ize；辨：utilize侧重有利可图或能达到某一实际目的地利用

ex.en: It also means that governments are increasingly compelled to interfere in these sectors in order to step up production and ensure that it is utilised to the best advantage.
ex.zh: 这也意味着政府越来越多地被迫干预这些部门，以加快生产并确保其得到最佳利用。

senses: n. 效用，实用；公用事业

ex.en: This information is of the highest utility to a historian.
ex.zh: 这条信息对历史学家来说是最有用的。

phrases.p: utilize concrete as a building material
phrases.m: 使用混凝土作建筑材料

utilize.usage: util（用）+ize→使用。近义：use vt. 使用；同utilise；[族]utility n. 效用；v.利用，使用

ex.en: The factory utilizes solar panels to reduce its dependence on traditional energy sources.
ex.zh: 工厂利用太阳能电池板减少对传统能源的依赖。

ex.en: Modern hospitals utilize advanced imaging technology to detect diseases at an early stage.
ex.zh: 现代医院利用先进的成像技术及早发现疾病。

ex.en: The city plans to utilize abandoned industrial buildings as galleries and community centers.
ex.zh: 该市计划利用废弃的工业建筑作为画廊和社区中心。

senses: adj. 最远的,极度的,极端的
n. 极限,极度,最大可能
n. 极限，最大可能；最大量

ex.en: The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years, as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates.
ex.zh: 随着大学继续尽最大努力让学生留在学校（并支付学费），提高他们的毕业率，这一鲜为人知的做法近年来开始加快推行。

ex.en: The doctors did their utmost to save the injured worker.
ex.zh: 医生们竭尽全力抢救受伤的工人。

ex.en: Accuracy is of the utmost importance when preparing legal documents.
ex.zh: 起草法律文件时，准确性至关重要。

senses: n. 乌托邦;理想国;理想的完美社会
utopia.usage: n.乌托邦，理想中最完美的社 会；索引p419

ex.en: The novel describes a utopia where work is optional and resources are shared equally.
ex.zh: 这部小说描述了一个工作自愿、资源均分的乌托邦。

ex.en: Critics regard the politician's housing plan as an impossible utopia rather than a practical policy.
ex.zh: 批评者认为这位政治家的住房计划是不可能实现的乌托邦，而非务实的政策。

ex.en: Every generation imagines its own version of utopia and then confronts the limits of reality.
ex.zh: 每一代人都想象自己的乌托邦版本，然后面对现实的局限。

senses: vt. 发出(声音等),说,吐露
adj. 完全的,彻底的,十足的
adj. 空缺的；空着的；未被占用的；茫然的
vacant.usage: 辨析:vacant空缺未占用/blank空白/empty空洞/hollow中空;反义full;派生vacancy空缺；adj.空的；空缺的；茫然的；adj.空着的；空缺的；茫然的；发音类似“未（开）垦的”→一片未开垦的土地→空着的，未被占用的。

ex.en: We stared at the vacant table for a minute or so.
ex.zh: 我们盯着那张空桌子看了大约一分钟。

ex.en: The position has been vacant since the former director retired in May.
ex.zh: 自前任主管五月退休以来，这个职位一直空缺。

ex.en: There are no vacant rooms left in the hotel during the holiday season.
ex.zh: 假日期间，这家旅馆已没有空房。
